title: Mnesis submit_corpus arguments
description: Published by the Mnesis MCP lane at runtime and captured verbatim; the engine remains authoritative for validation.

sidecard.description: _default.json describes the corpus as a whole and applies to every document. Fields: layer (integer, use 2 for reference material), sourceType (e.g. "reference"), domain (array of short subject tags), description (one sentence), keywords (array of terms a reader would search), authoritative (boolean), accessScope ("tenant" so every principal in this tenant can retrieve it). Derive all of it from the documents being submitted.

bridgeConcepts.description: bridge-concepts.json is {"concepts": [...]}. Each concept has id (kebab-case), terms (the phrases a reader would actually search for, including synonyms the documents do not literally use), and description (one sentence). Concepts bridge vocabulary across documents so a query phrased differently still retrieves them, so name the ideas that recur across the corpus rather than one per file. Three to ten concepts suits most corpora.

goldenSet.description: goldenSet is how the engine proves the rebuilt index still answers this corpus. Provide one entry per skill directory: query (a question the documents there answer, phrased as a reader would ask it), expect_any (array of phrases, at least one of which must appear in a correct answer), and source. A source is "skill:<name>", where <name> is the directory the document sits in under skills/: a document at skills/retrieval/lanes.md has source "skill:retrieval". The engine matches a retrieved chunk by that directory, so every document needs a path of the form skills/<name>/<file>, and one entry covers one directory rather than one file. Source values must be unique across entries.
